title: The Guest Too Large for the Universe
deck: A visitor from outside the cosmos is bending the stars of the Hesper cluster, three armed powers are turning their keys, and Illuminara has to find out whether what looks like an attack is a birth, in a way none of them has to take on trust.
shape: A convergent clock; each scene turns a claim into a prediction until four suspicious hands can read the answer on their own instruments.

scenes.title: The Nine Clocks
paragraphs: *Command deck, Kerrel's Anchor · Day one, 06:10*
Nine clocks hung on the forward bulkhead, and no two of them agreed.

The Kerrel Assembly kept them there on purpose, one for each inhabited system that still sent timing, so that its officers could see how far the sky had come apart. The spread was four minutes now. Yesterday it had been ninety seconds. Beyond the viewport the stars of the Hesper cluster sat a hair out of place, as though someone had jogged the table they stood on.
Commander Maren Vask met Illuminara at the lock with a slate in each hand and no greeting.

**Maren Vask**  
You have until ten-forty tomorrow morning. That is the Triple Key's deadline, not mine. Kerrel, the Ussu Chorus and the Halcyon fleet each hold a third of a strike order, and all three keys are turned to ready. At ten-forty the thing in the outer reach is hit with everything the Reach owns.

**Wren Odira**  
It has not fired on anyone. I would like that said before anybody says invader.

**Maren Vask**  
It has taken the tide-songs from two Ussu brood-worlds. It cost a convoy its navigation for six hours. It is a body the size of a small moon, and the sky bends where it sits. I do not need it to fire, Wren. I need it to stop.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will ask what you would ask. What is it doing, in order, and when? Not what it means. The log.

Nine entries. Each was a pulse: the stars within a light-year swung a few arcseconds off their places, hung there for about forty minutes, and swung back. Illuminara did not look at the swells. She looked at the gaps between them.

**Illuminara**  
Twelve hours. Ten and a half. Nine and a bit. Each gap is seven-eighths of the one before it.

**Maren Vask**  
A decaying signal. Alarms do that. So does a fuse.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. And a fuse has an end. The last gap was four hours forty-three, and seven times that is thirty-three hours. At about one tomorrow afternoon the gaps are shorter than the pulses, and the pulses run together into one. Your Key turns two hours and twenty minutes before that.
Nobody on the deck said anything. One of the nine clocks ticked over, three seconds ahead of its neighbour.

**Illuminara**  
It is an ending or a beginning. I do not know which, and neither do you. Before anything else I want a way of finding out that none of us has to take on faith.

scenes.title: Seven-Eighths
paragraphs: *Operations hall, Kerrel's Anchor · Day one, 07:40*

The delegates came by relay. Commander Vask for Kerrel. Iyo-Seven for the Ussu Chorus, seven bodies in a tide-tank who spoke by turns. Tally for the Halcyon fleet, a point of cold light on the table that answered in the flat, courteous voice of a machine that had decided long ago not to be liked.
Illuminara set two stories side by side and asked them to distrust both equally.

**Illuminara**  
Story one: a being from outside our cosmos is in labour. The gaps shorten because that is what labour does, and between pulses the strain falls back to the same floor, because between contractions a body rests. Story two: an incursion wearing a mother's shape. The gaps shorten because the weapon is nearly ready, and between pulses the floor would climb, because a thing that is charging does not rest.

**Maren Vask**  
Story two is the one a mother's story is built to hide.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. So I am not asking you to believe either. I am asking you to predict. Each of you measures the pulses with your own instruments and seals when the next one begins and how high the floor sits after it. Nobody opens an envelope until the pulse has come.

**Tally**  
Kerrel keeps time by atoms, the Chorus by song, my fleet by ranging pulsars. Our errors are unrelated. If all three of us land together, it will not be because we copied one another.

**Iyo-Seven**  
Each pulse unmakes the songs of our young. We do not ask for pity. We ask that your test be quick.

The tenth pulse began at 08:07 and held the sky for forty minutes. Tally had sealed 08:06, the Chorus 08:09, Kerrel 08:05. Behind the swell the floor dropped back to where it had dropped before, within the width of a pencil line.

**Maren Vask**  
Once. A coin can land once.

**Illuminara**  
A coin can. So we throw it again at every pulse, and we write down now what would make us stop. If the floor rises more than three parts in a hundred of the peak, or a gap breaks the seven-eighths by more than a quarter of itself, the story is false and the Key turns. We write that while none of us is frightened. We will not be able to write it when we are.
Tally logged the line without comment. After a moment so did Iyo-Seven, seven bodies nodding out of step. Vask took longest.

**Maren Vask**  
And while the coin is in the air, you intend to go and ask the thing itself.

**Illuminara**  
I intend to ask it what no instrument of yours can read.

**Wren Odira**  
I keep the clock. I say your name every hour. You answer, or I come in.

**Illuminara**  
You can't come into a window.

**Wren Odira**  
Watch me find out.

scenes.title: The Window
paragraphs: *Tide-boat Long Patience, outer reach · Day one, 09:20*

The Long Patience hung a light-year and a half from the guest, as near as the Ussu would take her. Illuminara felt the thing out in the dark as a slow tilt in the floor of everything, a hill her body leaned away from.

She made the window the way she had made them before, a place where one consciousness could meet another without either being crushed. She knew its limits as she knew her own hands: it could be widened to take a weight far larger than she was, for a while, and past a certain width it stopped being a window and became something that broke the one holding it. The guest came into it as a long dim shoreline, warm at the far end, with something at the warm end turning over in its sleep.

**Anomei**  
You are small, and not afraid enough. Good. The others sent engines.

**Illuminara**  
I am Illuminara. Are you hurting my cluster on purpose?

**Anomei**  
I am hurting it by being. You are a room, and I was offered a closet. At the first door they closed a gate. At the second they sang me away. At the third they sent a fleet. I did not come for your stars. I came for what I carry.

**Illuminara**  
Tell me what you carry.

**Anomei**  
A child. In your word, which is a poor word for it: soon.

**Anomei**  
I will tell you what I have told no one, because you asked and did not aim. If I am refused a place, I will bear the child where I stand. Its first breath will pour my home's law into your space: a core that takes everything it holds, and a fringe felt three light-years across. It will not be malice. It will be a birth. I would rather be the thing you fear than watch my child die in a closet.
Illuminara did not soften it. She had learned long ago that the worst thing to do with a true threat was to make it smaller for the people who had to decide about it.

**Illuminara**  
Then I will carry that sentence to three suspicious powers exactly as you said it. They need to know what refusing you costs, and they will believe the rest only if you have hidden nothing. In here I can widen the room to take some of what you spill, and whatever falls inside it does not press on the sky. I cannot take all of it, and I cannot do the part that is yours. What must the room outside be? Do not say large. Tell me how.
Anomei had no measure for it in any language Illuminara could translate. So she went to the stars.

Every star in the cluster had swung by an amount she could read, and every star had a known weight and distance. A body pressing on the sky should push the near stars hard and the far stars softly, falling away by a fixed rule. She laid the swings against the rule and asked what size of pressing thing would draw that curve. It came out as a core six-tenths of a light-year in radius at the first pulse and a little under one by the series' end. The fringe of the law would run half as far again beyond the core. The child was leaning on the walls of the room, and the lean grew by exactly as much as the wall was missing.
It was an inference, and the weakest thing she had. She marked it so, and searched her charts for a place empty to that radius and well past it.

**Illuminara**  
There is a void at the cluster's edge. Dornrath. Nothing in it larger than a comet for nearly two light-years in every direction.

**Anomei**  
At the second door they called it the ocean of nobody.

**Illuminara**  
It is not nobody's. Nine thousand people live on its rim, in the dark, on purpose. Asking them is the first thing I must do, and they can say no.

**Anomei**  
Then I must wait for an answer from strangers about my child. I have never asked a stranger for anything.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Here, Wren. Hour one. Here.

scenes.title: The Ocean of Nobody
paragraphs: *The Quiet Rung, rim of the Dornrath void · Day one, 12:15*

The eleventh pulse was still holding the sky when the Long Patience docked. The Tenders lived in the dark because they had wanted quiet, and three generations had not talked them out of it: nine thousand people on a ring of habitats lit by ice-farm glow. Tally read out Halcyon's survey as flatly as a ledger: empty to 1.9 light-years from the centre, one dead comet, no traffic.
Elder Pell Auro heard it standing, one hand on the rail of her council balcony.

**Pell Auro**  
So you have come to rent our dark.

**Illuminara**  
I have come to ask for it. I cannot rent what is not mine, and you may refuse.

**Pell Auro**  
And if I do?

**Illuminara**  
Then I go back to a table where three keys are turning and tell them to find another room. There is no other room. I will not pretend that costs you nothing to be asked.
Tally threw the floor trace on the wall: the swells rising, the floor underneath flat as a table. Pell looked at it for a long time.

**Pell Auro**  
I have borne four children. The floor goes flat. Between, you rest. You have to.

**Tally**  
A Tender's testimony cannot be entered as a measurement.

**Pell Auro**  
No. I am not a measurement. I am the owner.

**Illuminara**  
There is a risk, and I would rather say it than have you find it. I got the size of the room from how the stars swung. If I am wrong by a factor of two, the fringe of her law meets your rim.

**Pell Auro**  
Then you ask nine thousand people to stake their lives on your arithmetic.

**Illuminara**  
I ask you to check it.
Corin Daas kept the Rung's survey instruments, a slow-spoken man with ink to the wrists. He took the nine swings away for forty minutes and came back with a different number.

**Corin Daas**  
One point three, at the end of the series. Not a little under one.
His fit leaned hardest on the nearest star, the bright one the charts called Wick.

**Illuminara**  
Wick is a double. Its suns circle each other in nine days and swing together, but the chart lists the pair as one mass. Take it out and fit the other eight.
He did, with his lips moving.

**Corin Daas**  
Nought point nine seven.

**Illuminara**  
Then I was a little low and you were a good deal high, and the double was the whole difference. Use your figure, not mine.
Tally ran his corrected model back over the eleven pulses so far. It had called every swing to within two parts in a hundred, and she logged that figure beside his name.

**Pell Auro**  
On a void that is one point nine. And you still ask for the dark.

Illuminara laid the plan out for the Elder and, by relay, for Vask and Iyo-Seven. Only the end of the series could say whether this was a mother or a weapon, so the plan had to hold even if the worse story were true. The guest would come to Dornrath in five hops, hop one to hop five, each made in the rest between pulses, folded small and able to do nothing but travel. The fleets would hold at three light-years, so that if the story broke they would strike in the middle of an empty ocean, with nothing of theirs or the Tenders' within reach.

**Maren Vask**  
The Key has a deadline. Ten-forty.

**Illuminara**  
It turns when the floor rises or a gap breaks, as we wrote this morning, and on nothing else.

**Maren Vask**  
Then it waits on your conditions. There will be no second warning.

**Pell Auro**  
Not enough. Your three powers hold three sealed envelopes. We will hold a fourth. Corin reads the core on our instruments at every hop, not Halcyon's. If his projection of the core passes one point two before she crosses, she does not come in; at that size the fringe, half as far again, stands within a tenth of our glass. Once she is in, a woman in labour is not a thing I will shut a door on, so I will shut my own. The Rung has ice-cores under it deep enough for every soul on it, eleven minutes down. We drill it at ten tomorrow. If his figure passes one point two while she is inside, the word is Tally's call and my alarm, and my people go down. She stays, and your Key does not turn on our fear. It turns on your two conditions.

**Maren Vask**  
A fourth hand on the stop is a fourth hand that can stop it at the worst hop.

**Illuminara**  
Yes. It is also the only hand that belongs to the people nearest the harm. I would rather have a veto I cannot talk past than a yes I bought.
Vask looked at the flat line on the wall for as long as Pell had.

**Maren Vask**  
Write it.

**Pell Auro**  
The inner ring goes to your Kerrel transports for the day, with their children and their animals. And afterward, whatever the sphere leaves in my sky, we sit at the table when it is decided what happens to it. Not as witnesses. As a hand.

**Maren Vask**  
Done.

**Pell Auro**  
Tell her the dark is lent. Not given.

**Illuminara**  
I will tell her exactly that.

scenes.title: Five Windows
paragraphs: *The outer lanes · Day one, 15:33 to Day two, 01:30*

Hop one opened at 15:33, the instant the twelfth pulse released the sky. The guest folded small, and for forty-four minutes the Ussu tide-boats sang a line of steady space toward Dornrath, and the thing that could bend the stars crossed two light-years without bending anything. Vask's ships hung at the edges with their guns trained, as the guest herself had asked. After each pulse Corin sent his projection to all four envelopes: nought point nine eight, nought point nine seven, nought point nine eight. The floor stayed flat. The officers on the Anchor's deck had stopped saying story two.
The fifteenth pulse came eleven minutes early.
It came at 21:56 where all three predictions had said 22:07, and the sky tilted and held. On the Anchor's deck Vask's hand went to the Key before the thought did.

**Maren Vask**  
It is early. It broke the series.

**Tally**  
By nine per cent of a gap. The sealed limit is a quarter. The floor is flat.

**Illuminara**  
It is not my guess. It is in the tolerance we wrote this morning, when nobody was frightened. I wrote it for exactly this minute. Please hold your hand where it is.
The hand stayed. That crisis was over, and had been paid for in advance. The other one was not.

The early pulse had shifted the series. But the last window, before the seventeenth pulse, had been fifty-seven minutes and was now forty-three, and Anomei needed forty-nine to cross the final two light-years folded small. A flinch at either end would drop her into the sky of the Reach at full size, with the contractions less than an hour apart.

**Anomei**  
I cannot do it faster.

**Maren Vask**  
Then I close my ships along the line. If she falls out of the fold, I want something near enough to catch her.
Seven bodies in a tide-tank began to sing as one, for the first time in Illuminara's hearing.

**Iyo-Seven**  
No. Your wakes are the noise we cannot hold. We cannot move her; that is hers. But we can hold the strain steady along the last line so she need not bend around it, and only if the line is empty. It will cost us the songs of two more broods. We choose that. You pay the other half: your ships stay where they are, and your guns come off the guest for forty-one minutes.

**Maren Vask**  
You ask me to look away from the thing I was told to stop.

**Iyo-Seven**  
We ask you to trust three other watchers. Tally still ranges her. Corin still reads her. You will see her, Commander; you will only not be pointing. We know the difference between an engine and a creature that is trying.
Vask took longer than she had taken over anything that day. Then the guns came off.

Hop five opened at 00:42, and with the strain held steady along the line it took forty-one minutes. At 01:23 the guest unfolded at the heart of the Dornrath void with two minutes to spare, and the sky of the Reach, for the first time in four days, did not tilt.

scenes.title: The Cradle
paragraphs: *Dornrath void, the Quiet Rung · Day two, 12:20*

By noon the pulses had run together into one long swell with no floor beneath it, which the Key's conditions had foreseen. The three fleets held at the edge of the void with their keys turned and their hands still. Wren sat in the lock of the last tide-boat with a Halcyon clock on one knee and a Kerrel clock on the other, and for the first time she did not say Illuminara's name every hour. She said it every ten minutes.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Here.

Inside the window the shoreline had become a warmth the size of a world with a sharp, small pain at its centre. Illuminara did not do the birth. It was not hers. She held a place where Anomei could be as large as her labour needed, and where the small one at the centre could go on being small.
Then the pain sharpened, and Anomei, who had never asked a stranger for anything, did what a body does in that pain. She reached outward.

On the Rung, Corin's projection ran up through one point one and past one point two. Tally said so. At one point two the fringe stood within a tenth of the glass; at one point three it would touch it.

**Pell Auro**  
Cores.

One word, into the relay. Eight thousand people who had drilled it at ten that morning went down the ice-stairs in nine minutes, with children carried and animals led, and Pell Auro was the last on the steps. On the Anchor, Vask's hand lay on the Key. The floor was not rising and no gap had broken, so the Key did not turn. It was the first time in four days she had been glad of a rule she did not like.

**Anomei**  
I cannot hold it in. It is going out of me.

**Illuminara**  
Then put it in the room. I will widen.

**Anomei**  
It is mine to bear. I will not set it on you.

**Illuminara**  
It is yours to bear, and the room is mine to hold. What falls inside the window does not touch the sky. I cannot take it all and I will not take the part that is yours. Choose.
Anomei was silent for the length of one contraction. Then the shoreline leaned.

**Anomei**  
Yes. Hold the room.

Illuminara widened the window. The hill she had always leaned away from came down on her, and she opened the room wider than she had ever held it, to the edge she knew, where a window is still a window. It was the first thing in the whole story that nobody else could have done.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.
Nothing answered. On Wren's knees the two clocks ticked, a hair apart.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Here.
It was very faint. Wren breathed out and went on counting.

The Rung's records gave the order of it afterward. Dessa Marl, who kept the live trace on the glass-deck, wrote 12:53 on her slate for the minute the window stood wide and 12:54 for the minute Corin's figure turned, with the contraction at full strength. It had peaked at one point three one, and the outer glass crazed along its northern arc, with no one behind it. Then it fell for as long as the window stood wide, and stopped when the window narrowed at 12:57, a minute before the swell ended. She had written the times down before anyone said the window was closing.

Corin's model had called every one of the eleven earlier swings to within two parts in a hundred, and in none of them had the figure turned back before the swell ended. Tally laid the two curves side by side, minute by minute, the fall of the stars' swing and the width of the window, and they matched where nothing else had been changed. A model error would not have widened and narrowed with her. The rest of the labour was Anomei's, and she bore it.

The sealed predictions of the end of the series came in at 12:41, 12:58 and 13:11. The swell ended at 12:58. The child's first breath made a sphere of its home's law, and Tally measured the core at eighty-four hundredths of a light-year in radius. The fringe reached barely a light-year and a quarter, well short of the Rung. The sphere lay in the middle of the void, a warm bright pearl in the dark, and the strain on every star in the cluster let go at once like a held breath. On Wren's knees the Kerrel clock and the Halcyon clock, which had refused to agree for four days, ticked over together. In the Anchor's command deck the nine clocks were within a second of one another before Vask had finished turning her key back.

The Cradle Accord was settled that evening, in the window, with the Elder, the Commander, Iyo-Seven and Tally speaking to a mother who held her child in a sphere nobody else could enter. The sphere would shrink as the child's body learned the law of this cosmos; Tally projected forty years. Until then the Tenders would host them and hold a hand at every table. One beacon, read by all four parties, would carry messages to the child's family. No body could cross without the consent of all four.

**Anomei**  
You have put my family's door in four hands.

**Illuminara**  
Yes, but any hand may refuse a crossing, and the refusal goes to the other three and to you with its reason, and it dies in a year unless that hand renews it with a reason an instrument can still read. A fear is not a reason. A reading is. If you or the child dispute it, the readings go on the table, and a reason they no longer bear lapses. A hand can keep a door shut. It cannot forget that it is shut.

**Maren Vask**  
Tally will renew everything for ever. It is a machine.

**Tally**  
I will not renew a refusal I cannot justify. If I must write a reason every year, Commander, I will run out of reasons long before you do.

**Anomei**  
Hear what I give and what I keep. I give the four hands, the beacon and the year, because I am a stranger here and I asked a stranger for help and it was given. I keep my refusal of the word guest. My child was born in this sky. When she is grown, let her say what she is.
The shoreline softened, and what came into the window next was not an answer but a name, which Illuminara translated as best she could. It meant something close to Hold.

Afterward, on the rim, Wren found her standing at the glass, the cracked arc behind her and the dark in front of her with a small pearl in the middle of it. The Tenders had lost a stretch of glass and the Chorus the songs of four broods. Where the hill had pressed on Illuminara there was a bruise she would carry for a while. None of that was small.

**Wren Odira**  
You didn't make them trust her.

**Illuminara**  
No. I made it so they didn't have to.

**Wren Odira**  
Come and drink something hot.
Illuminara went.

critic_line: An extra-universal mother and four frightened polities freely choose a measurable, consent-bound cradle after Illuminara turns their strongest fear into a test, accepts a bounded physical burden and makes trust unnecessary for the rescue to succeed.

translation_sl.title: Gostja, prevelika za vesolje
translation_sl.deck: Obiskovalka iz prostora zunaj kozmosa ukrivlja zvezde jate Hesper, tri oborožene sile obračajo svoje ključe, Illuminara pa mora ugotoviti, ali je to, kar je videti kot napad, v resnici rojstvo — in to tako, da ji nikomur od njih ni treba verjeti na besedo.
translation_sl.shape: Konvergentna ura; vsak prizor spremeni trditev v napoved, dokler štiri nezaupljive roke odgovora ne morejo prebrati na lastnih instrumentih.

scenes.title: Devet ur
paragraphs: *Poveljniški most, Kerrel's Anchor · prvi dan, 06:10*
Na sprednji pregradi je viselo devet ur in niti dve se nista ujemali.

Skupščina Kerrel jih je tam hranila namenoma, po eno za vsak naseljeni sistem, ki je še vedno pošiljal časovne signale, da so častniki lahko videli, kako daleč se je nebo razmaknilo. Razlika je zdaj znašala štiri minute. Včeraj je bila devetdeset sekund. Za razglednim oknom so zvezde jate Hesper stale za las iz svojih mest, kakor da bi nekdo sunil mizo, na kateri so bile postavljene.
Poveljnica Maren Vask je Illuminaro pričakala pri zračni zapornici s tablico v vsaki roki in brez pozdrava.

**Maren Vask**  
Do jutri ob desetih štirideset imate čas. To je rok Trojnega ključa, ne moj. Kerrel, Zbor Ussu in flota Halcyon držijo vsak tretjino ukaza za napad, vsi trije ključi pa so obrnjeni v pripravljenost. Ob desetih štirideset bo stvar v zunanjem dosegu zadeta z vsem, kar Doseg premore.

**Wren Odira**  
Na nikogar ni streljala. Želim, da to povemo, preden jo kdo poimenuje napadalec.

**Maren Vask**  
Dvema zarodnima svetovoma Ussu je vzela plimske pesmi. Konvoj je zaradi nje šest ur ostal brez navigacije. Je telo velikosti majhne lune in nebo se ukrivlja tam, kjer sedi. Ni mi treba, da strelja, Wren. Potrebujem, da neha.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom vprašala, kar bi vprašali vi. Kaj počne, po vrsti, in kdaj? Ne kaj pomeni. Dnevnik.

Devet vnosov. Vsak je bil sunek: zvezde znotraj svetlobnega leta so se za nekaj ločnih sekund odmaknile od svojih mest, tam obstale približno štirideset minut in se vrnile. Illuminara ni gledala nabrekanj. Gledala je presledke med njimi.

**Illuminara**  
Dvanajst ur. Deset in pol. Nekaj več kot devet. Vsak presledek je sedem osmin prejšnjega.

**Maren Vask**  
Pojemajoč signal. Tako delujejo alarmi. Tudi vžigalna vrvica.

**Illuminara**  
Da. In vžigalna vrvica ima konec. Zadnji presledek je trajal štiri ure in triinštirideset minut, sedemkrat toliko pa je triintrideset ur. Jutri okoli ene popoldne bodo presledki krajši od sunkov in sunki se bodo zlili v enega. Vaš Ključ se obrne dve uri in dvajset minut prej.
Nihče na mostu ni nič rekel. Ena od devetih ur je preklopila, tri sekunde pred sosednjo.

**Illuminara**  
To je konec ali začetek. Ne vem kateri in tudi vi ne. Pred vsem drugim želim način, da to ugotovimo, ne da bi moral kdorkoli od nas verjeti na besedo.

scenes.title: Sedem osmin
paragraphs: *Operativna dvorana, Kerrel's Anchor · prvi dan, 07:40*

Delegati so prišli po releju. Poveljnica Vask za Kerrel. Iyo-Seven za Zbor Ussu, sedem teles v plimskem rezervoarju, ki so govorila izmenično. Tally za floto Halcyon, točka hladne svetlobe na mizi, ki je odgovarjala z ravnim, vljudnim glasom stroja, ki se je že zdavnaj odločil, da mu ni treba biti všečen.
Illuminara je postavila dve zgodbi drugo ob drugo in jih prosila, naj obema enako ne zaupajo.

**Illuminara**  
Prva zgodba: bitje iz prostora zunaj našega kozmosa rojeva. Presledki se krajšajo, ker porod tako deluje, med sunki pa napetost pade nazaj na isto dno, ker telo med popadki počiva. Druga zgodba: vdor v materinski podobi. Presledki se krajšajo, ker je orožje skoraj pripravljeno, med sunki pa bi se dno dvigovalo, ker stvar, ki se polni, ne počiva.

**Maren Vask**  
Druga zgodba je tisto, kar naj bi zgodba o materi prikrila.

**Illuminara**  
Da. Zato vas ne prosim, da verjamete kateri od njiju. Prosim vas, da napoveste. Vsak meri sunke s svojimi instrumenti ter zapečati, kdaj se bo začel naslednji in kako visoko bo dno po njem. Nihče ne odpre ovojnice, dokler sunek ne pride.

**Tally**  
Kerrel meri čas z atomi, Zbor s pesmijo, moja flota z razdaljami do pulzarjev. Naše napake niso povezane. Če vsi trije pridemo do istega rezultata, ne bo zato, ker bi prepisovali drug od drugega.

**Iyo-Seven**  
Vsak sunek razdere pesmi naših mladičev. Ne prosimo za usmiljenje. Prosimo, da je vaš preizkus hiter.

Deseti sunek se je začel ob 08:07 in držal nebo štirideset minut. Tally je zapečatila 08:06, Zbor 08:09, Kerrel 08:05. Za nabrekanjem je dno padlo nazaj tja, kamor je padlo prej, znotraj širine črte svinčnika.

**Maren Vask**  
Enkrat. Kovanec lahko enkrat tako pade.

**Illuminara**  
Kovanec lahko. Zato ga vržemo znova ob vsakem sunku in zdaj zapišemo, kaj nas bo ustavilo. Če se dno dvigne za več kot tri stotinke vrha ali če presledek odstopi od sedmih osmin za več kot četrtino samega sebe, je zgodba napačna in Ključ se obrne. To napišemo, ko nikogar od nas ni strah. Ko nas bo, tega ne bomo mogli napisati.
Tally je vrstico zabeležila brez pripombe. Čez trenutek jo je tudi Iyo-Seven, sedem teles je prikimavalo neusklajeno. Vask je potrebovala najdlje.

**Maren Vask**  
In medtem ko je kovanec v zraku, nameravate oditi in vprašati samo stvar.

**Illuminara**  
Vprašala jo bom nekaj, česar noben vaš instrument ne more prebrati.

**Wren Odira**  
Jaz držim uro. Vsako uro izgovorim vaše ime. Odgovorite ali pa pridem noter.

**Illuminara**  
Ne moreš priti v okno.

**Wren Odira**  
Glej me, kako bom preverila.

scenes.title: Okno
paragraphs: *Plimski čoln Long Patience, zunanji doseg · prvi dan, 09:20*

Long Patience je visel svetlobno leto in pol od gostje, tako blizu, kot so jo bili Ussu pripravljeni odpeljati. Illuminara je stvar v temi čutila kot počasen nagib tal vsega, hrib, od katerega se je njeno telo nagibalo proč.

Okno je naredila tako, kot jih je delala že prej, prostor, kjer se je ena zavest lahko srečala z drugo, ne da bi bila katera zdrobljena. Njegove meje je poznala, kakor je poznala lastne roke: za nekaj časa ga je bilo mogoče razširiti, da sprejme težo, veliko večjo od nje, čez določeno širino pa je prenehalo biti okno in postalo nekaj, kar zlomi tistega, ki ga drži. Gostja je vanj vstopila kakor dolga medla obala, topla na oddaljenem koncu, na toplem koncu pa se je nekaj obračalo v spanju.

**Anomei**  
Majhna si in premalo te je strah. Dobro. Drugi so poslali motorje.

**Illuminara**  
Sem Illuminara. Ali mojo jato prizadeneš namenoma?

**Anomei**  
Prizadenem jo s tem, da sem. Ti si soba, meni pa so ponudili omaro. Pri prvih vratih so zaprli zaporo. Pri drugih so me s pesmijo odgnali. Pri tretjih so poslali floto. Nisem prišla po vaše zvezde. Prišla sem zaradi tega, kar nosim.

**Illuminara**  
Povej mi, kaj nosiš.

**Anomei**  
Otroka. Z vašo besedo, ki je za to slaba beseda: kmalu.

**Anomei**  
Povedala ti bom, česar nisem povedala nikomur, ker si vprašala in nisi merila vame. Če mi odrečejo prostor, bom otroka rodila tam, kjer stojim. Njegov prvi vdih bo v vaš prostor izlil zakon mojega doma: jedro, ki vzame vse, kar drži, in rob, ki ga bo čutiti tri svetlobna leta naokrog. To ne bo zloba. To bo rojstvo. Raje postanem stvar, ki se je bojite, kot da bi gledala, kako moj otrok umre v omari.
Illuminara grožnje ni olepšala. Že davno se je naučila, da je najslabše, kar lahko storiš z resnično grožnjo, to, da jo pomanjšaš za ljudi, ki morajo o njej odločati.

**Illuminara**  
Potem bom ta stavek trem nezaupljivim silam prenesla natanko tako, kot si ga izrekla. Vedeti morajo, koliko jih bo stala zavrnitev, vse drugo pa bodo verjeli le, če nisi ničesar skrila. Tukaj lahko razširim sobo, da prevzame del tega, kar razliješ, in kar pade vanjo, ne pritiska na nebo. Ne morem prevzeti vsega in ne morem opraviti dela, ki je tvoje. Kakšna mora biti zunanja soba? Ne reci velika. Povej mi kako.
Anomei za to ni imela mere v nobenem jeziku, ki bi ga Illuminara lahko prevedla. Zato se je obrnila k zvezdam.

Vsaka zvezda v jati se je premaknila za količino, ki jo je lahko prebrala, vsaka pa je imela znano maso in razdaljo. Telo, ki pritiska na nebo, bi moralo bližnje zvezde potisniti močno, oddaljene pa šibko, po nespremenljivem pravilu pojemanja. Premike je položila ob pravilo in vprašala, kakšna velikost pritiskajoče stvari bi zarisala takšno krivuljo. Rezultat je bil jedro s polmerom šest desetin svetlobnega leta ob prvem sunku in nekaj manj kot eno svetlobno leto ob koncu zaporedja. Rob zakona bi segel še polovico te razdalje čez jedro. Otrok se je naslanjal na stene sobe in pritisk je rasel natanko za toliko, kolikor stene ni bilo.
To je bilo sklepanje in najšibkejša stvar, ki jo je imela. Tako ga je tudi označila in na kartah poiskala kraj, prazen do tega polmera in daleč onkraj njega.

**Illuminara**  
Na robu jate je praznina. Dornrath. Skoraj dve svetlobni leti v vse smeri ni v njej ničesar, večjega od kometa.

**Anomei**  
Pri drugih vratih so ji rekli ocean nikogar.

**Illuminara**  
Ni nikogaršnja. Na njenem robu živi devet tisoč ljudi, v temi, namenoma. Najprej moram vprašati njih in lahko rečejo ne.

**Anomei**  
Potem moram čakati na odgovor tujcev o svojem otroku. Tujca še nikoli nisem prosila za nič.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Tukaj, Wren. Prva ura. Tukaj.

scenes.title: Ocean nikogar
paragraphs: *Quiet Rung, rob praznine Dornrath · prvi dan, 12:15*

Enajsti sunek je še držal nebo, ko je Long Patience pristal. Skrbniki so živeli v temi, ker so si želeli miru, in tri generacije jih niso prepričale o nasprotnem: devet tisoč ljudi na obroču bivališč, osvetljenih s sijem ledenih kmetij. Tally je Halcyonovo raziskavo prebrala enolično kakor knjigovodski zapis: prazno do 1,9 svetlobnega leta od središča, en mrtev komet, brez prometa.
Starešina Pell Auro je to poslušala stoje, z eno roko na ograji svojega svetniškega balkona.

**Pell Auro**  
Torej ste prišli najeti našo temo.

**Illuminara**  
Prišla sem prosit zanjo. Ne morem najeti nečesa, kar ni moje, vi pa lahko zavrnete.

**Pell Auro**  
In če zavrnem?

**Illuminara**  
Potem se vrnem k mizi, kjer se obračajo trije ključi, in jim naročim, naj poiščejo drugo sobo. Druge sobe ni. Ne bom se pretvarjala, da vas to vprašanje nič ne stane.
Tally je na steno projicirala sled dna: nabrekanja so se dvigala, dno pod njimi pa je bilo ravno kakor miza. Pell jo je dolgo gledala.

**Pell Auro**  
Rodila sem štiri otroke. Dno postane ravno. Vmes počivaš. Moraš.

**Tally**  
Pričevanja Skrbnice ni mogoče vpisati kot meritev.

**Pell Auro**  
Ne. Nisem meritev. Sem lastnica.

**Illuminara**  
Obstaja tveganje in raje ga povem, kot da ga odkrijete sami. Velikost sobe sem izračunala iz premikov zvezd. Če se motim za faktor dve, rob njenega zakona doseže vaš obroč.

**Pell Auro**  
Potem devet tisoč ljudi prosite, naj življenje zastavijo na vašo aritmetiko.

**Illuminara**  
Prosim vas, da jo preverite.
Corin Daas je skrbel za raziskovalne instrumente obroča, počasen govorec s črnilom do zapestij. Devet premikov je za štirideset minut odnesel s seboj in se vrnil z drugo številko.

**Corin Daas**  
Ena cela tri ob koncu zaporedja. Ne nekaj manj kot ena.
Njegovo prileganje se je najmočneje opiralo na najbližjo zvezdo, svetlo, ki so jo karte imenovale Wick.

**Illuminara**  
Wick je dvojna. Njeni sonci drug okoli drugega krožita v devetih dneh in se premikata skupaj, karta pa par navaja kot eno maso. Izločite jo in prilegajte ostalih osem.
To je storil, ustnice so se mu premikale.

**Corin Daas**  
Nič cela devet sedem.

**Illuminara**  
Potem sem bila jaz malo prenizka, vi pa precej previsoki, dvojna zvezda pa je bila vsa razlika. Uporabite svojo številko, ne moje.
Tally je njegov popravljeni model pognala nazaj čez vseh enajst dosedanjih sunkov. Vsak premik je napovedal na dve stotinki natančno in to številko je zabeležila ob njegovem imenu.

**Pell Auro**  
V praznini, veliki ena cela devet. In še vedno prosite za temo.

Illuminara je načrt razgrnila pred starešino ter po releju pred Vask in Iyo-Seven. Le konec zaporedja bi lahko povedal, ali je to mati ali orožje, zato je moral načrt zdržati tudi, če bi bila slabša zgodba resnična. Gostja bi v Dornrath prišla v petih skokih, od prvega do petega, vsakem med počitkom med sunki, zložena na majhno in sposobna samo potovanja. Flote bi obstale tri svetlobna leta proč, da bi v primeru, če bi se zgodba prelomila, udarile sredi praznega oceana, ko nič njihovega ali skrbniškega ne bi bilo v dosegu.

**Maren Vask**  
Ključ ima rok. Deset štirideset.

**Illuminara**  
Obrne se, ko se dno dvigne ali ko se presledek prelomi, kakor smo zapisali zjutraj, in zaradi ničesar drugega.

**Maren Vask**  
Potem čaka na vaše pogoje. Drugega opozorila ne bo.

**Pell Auro**  
Ni dovolj. Vaše tri sile držijo tri zapečatene ovojnice. Mi bomo držali četrto. Corin bo jedro ob vsakem skoku odčital na naših instrumentih, ne Halcyonovih. Če njegova projekcija jedra preseže ena cela dve, preden prečka mejo, ne pride noter; pri tej velikosti rob, ki seže še polovico dlje, stoji desetinko svetlobnega leta od našega stekla. Ko bo enkrat noter, porodnice ne bom izgnala, zato bom zaprla lastna vrata. Pod obročem so ledena jedra dovolj globoko za vsako dušo na njem, enajst minut navzdol. Vajo bomo izvedli jutri ob desetih. Če njegova številka preseže ena cela dve, ko bo že noter, bo beseda Tallyjin klic in moj alarm, moji ljudje pa bodo odšli dol. Ona ostane in vaš Ključ se ne obrne zaradi našega strahu. Obrne se zaradi vaših dveh pogojev.

**Maren Vask**  
Četrta roka na zaustavitvi je četrta roka, ki jo lahko ustavi pri najslabšem skoku.

**Illuminara**  
Da. Je tudi edina roka, ki pripada ljudem, najbližjim nevarnosti. Raje imam veto, ki ga ne morem pregovoriti, kot privolitev, ki sem jo kupila.
Vask je ravno črto na steni gledala tako dolgo, kot jo je Pell.

**Maren Vask**  
Zapišite.

**Pell Auro**  
Notranji obroč gre za ta dan vašim kerrelskim transportom, skupaj z otroki in živalmi. In potem, karkoli bo krogla pustila na mojem nebu, bomo sedeli za mizo, ko se bo odločalo, kaj se bo z njim zgodilo. Ne kot priče. Kot roka.

**Maren Vask**  
Dogovorjeno.

**Pell Auro**  
Povejte ji, da je tema posojena. Ne podarjena.

**Illuminara**  
Povedala ji bom natanko tako.

scenes.title: Pet oken
paragraphs: *Zunanji koridorji · prvi dan, 15:33, do drugega dne, 01:30*

Prvi skok se je odprl ob 15:33, v trenutku, ko je dvanajsti sunek izpustil nebo. Gostja se je zložila na majhno in plimski čolni Ussu so štiriinštirideset minut peli črto mirnega prostora proti Dornrathu, stvar, ki je lahko ukrivila zvezde, pa je prečkala dve svetlobni leti, ne da bi ukrivila karkoli. Vaskine ladje so visele na robovih z uperjenimi topovi, kakor je prosila sama gostja. Po vsakem sunku je Corin v vse štiri ovojnice poslal svojo projekcijo: nič cela devet osem, nič cela devet sedem, nič cela devet osem. Dno je ostalo ravno. Častniki na mostu Anchorja so nehali govoriti druga zgodba.
Petnajsti sunek je prišel enajst minut prezgodaj.
Prišel je ob 21:56, ko so vse tri napovedi kazale 22:07, nebo pa se je nagnilo in obstalo. Na mostu Anchorja je Vaskina roka segla po Ključu, še preden je misel.

**Maren Vask**  
Prezgodaj je. Prelomila je zaporedje.

**Tally**  
Za devet odstotkov presledka. Zapečatena meja je četrtina. Dno je ravno.

**Illuminara**  
To ni moja domneva. Je znotraj tolerance, ki smo jo zapisali zjutraj, ko nikogar ni bilo strah. Zapisala sem jo prav za to minuto. Prosim, obdržite roko tam, kjer je.
Roka je ostala. Ta kriza je minila in zanjo so plačali vnaprej. Za drugo niso.

Zgodnji sunek je premaknil zaporedje. Toda zadnje okno pred sedemnajstim sunkom je prej trajalo sedeminpetdeset minut, zdaj pa triinštirideset, Anomei pa je potrebovala devetinštirideset minut, da bi zložena na majhno prečkala zadnji dve svetlobni leti. Trzljaj na kateremkoli koncu bi jo v polni velikosti odložil v nebo Dosega, popadki pa bi bili manj kot uro narazen.

**Anomei**  
Ne morem hitreje.

**Maren Vask**  
Potem svoje ladje strnem vzdolž črte. Če pade iz zgiba, želim nekaj dovolj blizu, da jo ujame.
Sedem teles v plimskem rezervoarju je začelo peti kot eno, prvič, odkar jih je Illuminara slišala.

**Iyo-Seven**  
Ne. Vaše sledi so hrup, ki ga ne moremo držati. Premakniti je ne moremo; to je njeno. Lahko pa vzdolž zadnje črte držimo napetost enakomerno, da se ji okoli nje ni treba ukrivljati, in samo, če je črta prazna. To nas bo stalo pesmi še dveh zarodov. To izberemo. Vi plačate drugo polovico: vaše ladje ostanejo, kjer so, topove pa za enainštirideset minut umaknete z gostje.

**Maren Vask**  
Prosite me, naj pogledam stran od stvari, ki naj bi jo ustavila.

**Iyo-Seven**  
Prosimo vas, da zaupate trem drugim opazovalcem. Tally jo še vedno meri. Corin jo še vedno bere. Videli jo boste, poveljnica; le merili ne boste vanjo. Poznamo razliko med motorjem in bitjem, ki se trudi.
Vask je potrebovala dlje kot pri čemerkoli tistega dne. Nato so se topovi umaknili.

Peti skok se je odprl ob 00:42 in z enakomerno zadržano napetostjo vzdolž črte je trajal enainštirideset minut. Ob 01:23 se je gostja razprla v srcu praznine Dornrath z dvema minutama rezerve, nebo Dosega pa se prvič po štirih dneh ni nagnilo.

scenes.title: Zibelka
paragraphs: *Praznina Dornrath, Quiet Rung · drugi dan, 12:20*

Do poldneva so se sunki zlili v eno dolgo nabrekanje brez dna pod seboj, kakor so predvideli pogoji Ključa. Tri flote so vztrajale na robu praznine z obrnjenimi ključi in mirnimi rokami. Wren je sedela v zapornici zadnjega plimskega čolna s halcyonovsko uro na enem kolenu in kerrelsko na drugem, prvič pa Illuminarinega imena ni izgovorila vsako uro. Izgovorila ga je vsakih deset minut.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Tukaj.

V oknu je obala postala toplota velikosti sveta z ostro, drobno bolečino v središču. Illuminara ni opravila rojstva. Ni bilo njeno. Držala je prostor, v katerem je bila Anomei lahko tako velika, kot je potreboval njen porod, in v katerem je lahko majhna v sredini ostala majhna.
Nato se je bolečina izostrila in Anomei, ki tujca še nikoli ni prosila za nič, je storila to, kar telo stori v takšni bolečini. Segla je navzven.

Na obroču je Corinova projekcija stekla čez ena cela ena in mimo ena cela dve. Tally je to povedala. Pri ena cela dve je rob stal desetinko svetlobnega leta od stekla; pri ena cela tri bi se ga dotaknil.

**Pell Auro**  
Jedra.

Ena beseda v rele. Osem tisoč ljudi, ki so vajo opravili ob desetih zjutraj, se je v devetih minutah spustilo po ledenih stopnicah, z otroki v naročju in živalmi na povodcih, Pell Auro pa je bila zadnja na stopnicah. Na Anchorju je Vaskina roka ležala na Ključu. Dno se ni dvigovalo in noben presledek se ni prelomil, zato se Ključ ni obrnil. Prvič v štirih dneh je bila vesela pravila, ki ji ni bilo všeč.

**Anomei**  
Ne morem ga zadržati. Teče iz mene.

**Illuminara**  
Potem ga položi v sobo. Razširila jo bom.

**Anomei**  
Moje je, da ga nosim. Ne bom ga položila nate.

**Illuminara**  
Tvoje je, da ga nosiš, sobo pa držim jaz. Kar pade v okno, se ne dotakne neba. Ne morem prevzeti vsega in ne bom prevzela dela, ki je tvoj. Izberi.
Anomei je molčala ves čas enega popadka. Nato se je obala nagnila.

**Anomei**  
Da. Drži sobo.

Illuminara je razširila okno. Hrib, od katerega se je vedno nagibala proč, se je zgrnil nanjo, ona pa je sobo odprla širše, kot jo je držala kadarkoli prej, vse do meje, ki jo je poznala, kjer je okno še vedno okno. To je bila prva stvar v vsej zgodbi, ki je ni mogel storiti nihče drug.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.
Nič ni odgovorilo. Na Wreninih kolenih sta uri tiktakali z drobcenim razmikom.

**Wren Odira**  
Illuminara.

**Illuminara**  
Tukaj.
Bilo je komaj slišno. Wren je izdihnila in štela naprej.

Zapisi obroča so pozneje podali vrstni red. Dessa Marl, ki je nadzirala živo sled na steklenem krovu, je na svojo tablico zapisala 12:53 za minuto, ko je okno stalo na široko, in 12:54 za minuto, ko se je Corinova številka ob polni moči popadka obrnila. Vrh je dosegla pri ena cela tri ena, zunanje steklo pa je vzdolž severnega loka drobno razpokalo, ko za njim ni bilo nikogar. Nato je številka padala toliko časa, kolikor je okno ostalo široko, in se ustavila, ko se je okno ob 12:57 zožilo, minuto preden se je nabrekanje končalo. Čase je zapisala, preden je kdorkoli rekel, da se okno zapira.

Corinov model je vseh enajst prejšnjih premikov napovedal na dve stotinki natančno in pri nobenem se številka ni obrnila nazaj pred koncem nabrekanja. Tally je obe krivulji položila drugo ob drugo, minuto za minuto, upad premika zvezd in širino okna, ujemali pa sta se tam, kjer se ni spremenilo nič drugega. Napaka modela se ne bi širila in ožila z njo. Preostanek poroda je bil Anomeijin in ona ga je prestala.

Zapečatene napovedi konca zaporedja so bile 12:41, 12:58 in 13:11. Nabrekanje se je končalo ob 12:58. Otrokov prvi vdih je ustvaril kroglo zakona njegovega doma, Tally pa je izmerila polmer jedra štiriinosemdeset stotink svetlobnega leta. Rob je segel komaj svetlobno leto in četrt, daleč pred obročem. Krogla je ležala sredi praznine, topel svetel biser v temi, napetost na vsaki zvezdi v jati pa je popustila naenkrat kakor zadržan dih. Na Wreninih kolenih sta kerrellska in halcyonovska ura, ki se štiri dni nista hoteli ujemati, hkrati preklopili. Na poveljniškem mostu Anchorja je devet ur kazalo v razmiku ene sekunde, še preden je Vask končala obračanje svojega ključa nazaj.

Sporazum o zibelki je bil sklenjen tistega večera v oknu, kjer so starešina, poveljnica, Iyo-Seven in Tally govorili z materjo, ki je svojega otroka držala v krogli, v katero ni mogel vstopiti nihče drug. Krogla bi se krčila, ko bi se otrokovo telo učilo zakona tega kozmosa; Tally je napovedala štirideset let. Do takrat bi ju gostili Skrbniki in imeli roko za vsako mizo. En svetilnik, ki bi ga brale vse štiri strani, bi prenašal sporočila otrokovi družini. Nobeno telo ne bi moglo prečkati brez soglasja vseh štirih.

**Anomei**  
Vrata moje družine ste položili v štiri roke.

**Illuminara**  
Da, vendar lahko katerakoli roka prehod zavrne, zavrnitev pa skupaj z razlogom prejmejo preostale tri in ti; čez leto preneha veljati, razen če jo ta roka obnovi z razlogom, ki ga instrument še vedno lahko prebere. Strah ni razlog. Odčitek je. Če ga ti ali otrok izpodbijata, se odčitki položijo na mizo in razlog, ki ga ne podpirajo več, preneha veljati. Roka lahko vrata obdrži zaprta. Ne more pozabiti, da so zaprta.

**Maren Vask**  
Tally bo vse obnavljala za vedno. Stroj je.

**Tally**  
Ne bom obnovila zavrnitve, ki je ne morem upravičiti. Če moram vsako leto zapisati razlog, poveljnica, mi jih bo zmanjkalo veliko prej kot vam.

**Anomei**  
Slišite, kaj dajem in kaj obdržim. Dajem štiri roke, svetilnik in leto, ker sem tukaj tujka ter sem tujca prosila za pomoč in mi jo je dal. Obdržim svojo zavrnitev besede gostja. Moj otrok se je rodil na tem nebu. Ko odraste, naj sama pove, kaj je.
Obala se je omehčala in v okno nato ni prišel odgovor, temveč ime, ki ga je Illuminara prevedla, kolikor je znala. Pomenilo je nekaj blizu besedi Drži.

Pozneje jo je Wren na robu našla stati ob steklu, z razpokanim lokom za njo in temo pred njo, z majhnim biserom v sredini. Skrbniki so izgubili pas stekla, Zbor pa pesmi štirih zarodov. Tam, kjer je hrib pritisnil na Illuminaro, je ostala modrica, ki jo bo nosila nekaj časa. Nič od tega ni bilo majhno.

**Wren Odira**  
Nisi dosegla, da bi ji zaupali.

**Illuminara**  
Ne. Poskrbela sem, da jim ni bilo treba.

**Wren Odira**  
Pridi popit nekaj vročega.
Illuminara je šla.
